{
  "summary": "Start descriptor key expansion in TopUpWithDB at the descriptor's range_start rather than index 0, and record the actual cached index instead of incrementing from -1. This ensures newly imported descriptors with non-zero range starts do not derive or track keys outside their specified range.",
  "problem": "When importing a descriptor with a range [N, M], TopUpWithDB begins deriving keys from index 0 up to M instead of N to M. This causes import costs to scale with M instead of the range length M - N, falsely marks scriptPubKeys below N as IsMine during import, drops those scriptPubKeys upon reopening the wallet (causing rescanned transactions below N to lose IsMine status), and causes active descriptors to re-expand their range on reload due to an inconsistent cached index counter.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description benchmarks: 'Importing wpkh(xpub/0/*) with \"range\": [600000, 600009] into a blank watch-only wallet goes from 19.5s to 0.09s on this machine.'",
    "PR description explains behavioral inconsistency: 'Load() only expands [range_start, range_end), so those scriptPubKeys stop being IsMine the next time the wallet is opened, and a transaction picked up for one of them during the import rescan is no longer credited to the wallet.'"

result.summary: Start descriptor key expansion in TopUpWithDB at the descriptor's range_start rather than index 0, and record the actual cached index instead of incrementing from -1. This ensures newly imported descriptors with non-zero range starts do not derive or track keys outside their specified range.
result.problem: When importing a descriptor with a range [N, M], TopUpWithDB begins deriving keys from index 0 up to M instead of N to M. This causes import costs to scale with M instead of the range length M - N, falsely marks scriptPubKeys below N as IsMine during import, drops those scriptPubKeys upon reopening the wallet (causing rescanned transactions below N to lose IsMine status), and causes active descriptors to re-expand their range on reload due to an inconsistent cached index counter.
evidence: PR description benchmarks: 'Importing wpkh(xpub/0/*) with "range": [600000, 600009] into a blank watch-only wallet goes from 19.5s to 0.09s on this machine.'

PR description explains behavioral inconsistency: 'Load() only expands [range_start, range_end), so those scriptPubKeys stop being IsMine the next time the wallet is opened, and a transaction picked up for one of them during the import rescan is no longer credited to the wallet.'
result.card: Ensures descriptor key expansion starts at range_start rather than index 0 during wallet top-ups. Currently, importing a descriptor with a range [N, M] derives and tracks all keys from 0 to M, causing O(M) import times, potential hangs or massive memory use for high range starts, and state divergence where scriptPubKeys below N are temporarily treated as owned until the wallet is reopened. The author notes that importing a 10-key range starting at index 600,000 drops from 19.5 seconds to 0.09 seconds.
